published_by: Ofgem (Default Tariff Cap) + HM Government (Energy Price Guarantee)
what_this_is: THE LAW, NOT A READING OF IT. The published cap-window boundaries and the published typical-household unit rates for each window, plus the EPG overlay where it was in force. Nothing here interprets the law: no carry-forward rule, no min() selection, no segment filter, no basis conversion. Those are READINGS and each lane owns its own.

basis.conversion: Ofgem publishes p/kWh typical-household unit rates; p/kWh x 10 = GBP/MWh
basis.standing_charge: EXCLUDED - this is a unit-rate ceiling only (R14: the basis travels with the figure)

window_boundaries_source: https://www.ofgem.gov.uk/energy-regulation/domestic-and-non-domestic/energy-pricing-rules/energy-price-cap/energy-price-cap-default-tariff-levels - six-monthly Apr/Oct from 1 Jan 2019 through 30 Sep 2022, quarterly from 1 Oct 2022
unit_rate_source: Published typical-household p/kWh per cap period (electricityprices.org.uk cap history). The Oct-2021 20.8p/4.07p and Apr-2022 28.34p/7.37p levels are independently corroborated by House of Commons Library CBP-9714 ('20.8p -> 28.3p electricity, 4.1p -> 7.4p gas'). Full sourcing: docs/market_research/ofgem_cap_windows.md
epg_note: Between Oct-2022 and Jun-2023 the Energy Price Guarantee held a typical dual-fuel bill at GBP 2,500, well below the Ofgem cap (which peaked at GBP 4,279 for Jan-Mar 2023). Both instruments are published separately here rather than pre-combined, so that a lane which fails to notice the EPG is a lane that MISREAD the law rather than a lane that was handed a different law.
r13_wall: Every date and level here is real published regulatory history, sourced blind to company P&L. No value in this file may be moved because a simulation result looks wrong.
portability: A schedule of windows, not a set of year branches. A second market or a changed regime supplies its own artefact behind the same loaders.
